title: Real conditions: si llueve, nos quedamos
summary: Talk about what happens if something real happens, using si + present and then a present, a future, an order or a plan.
focus: Real conditions: si + present indicative with a present, future, imperative or ir a / poder / tener que result
content:
## Si + present: real possibilities

**Si** (if, no accent) introduces a condition that can really happen. In a real condition the **si**-half always takes the **present indicative**, even when it is about tomorrow.

When the result is always true (a general rule, a habit), the other half is in the present too:

- **Si llueve, me mojo.** If it rains, I get wet.
- **Si mezclas rojo y blanco, sale rosa.** If you mix red and white, you get pink.
- **Si llego tarde, mi jefe se enfada.** If I'm late, my boss gets cross.

Spelling: **si** = if; **sí** with an accent = yes. **Sí, voy si puedo.** Yes, I'll go if I can.

## The other half: future, order or plan

The **si**-half stays in the present, and the result can take several shapes:

| result | example |
|---|---|
| present (near future) | **Si llueve mañana, nos quedamos en casa.** If it rains tomorrow, we'll stay at home. |
| future | **Si estudias, aprobarás.** If you study, you'll pass. |
| imperative | **Si tienes tiempo, llámame.** If you have time, call me. |
| ir a + infinitive | **Si sale bien, vamos a celebrarlo.** If it goes well, we're going to celebrate. |
| poder / tener que | **Si pierdes el tren, puedes coger el siguiente.** If you miss the train, you can catch the next one. |

## Which half first? The comma

Either half can go first. The meaning stays the same; the punctuation changes:

- **si**-half first: a comma after it: **Si tienes frío, cierra la ventana.**
- **si**-half second: no comma: **Cierra la ventana si tienes frío.**

Starting with **si** sets the scene first ("this is the situation"); starting with the result puts the news first. Both orders are everyday Spanish.

## Never the future or the subjunctive after si

English says *if it rains*, not *if it will rain*. Spanish is the same, and stricter:

- Write **Si llueve**, no salimos, not ~~Si lloverá~~.
- Write **Si tienes tiempo**, ven, not ~~Si tengas tiempo~~.

(After **no sé si** = *whether*, the future is fine: **No sé si vendrá.** That **si** is not a condition.)

The subjunctive does turn up with **en caso de que** (in case), which always takes it: **Lleva el paraguas en caso de que llueva.** Take the umbrella in case it rains.

Unlikely or impossible conditions (*if I were rich…*) are coming at B2.

vocabulary.example: Si quieres, te acompaño a casa.
vocabulary.example_meaning: If you like, I'll walk you home.

vocabulary.example: Te dejo mi número en caso de que necesites algo.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I'll leave you my number in case you need anything.

vocabulary.example: Si llueve el domingo, vemos una película en casa.
vocabulary.example_meaning: If it rains on Sunday, we'll watch a film at home.

vocabulary.example: Si sales sin abrigo, te vas a mojar.
vocabulary.example_meaning: If you go out without a coat, you're going to get wet.

vocabulary.example: Si estás cansada, quédate en el sofá.
vocabulary.example_meaning: If you're tired, stay on the sofa.

vocabulary.example: Si practicas cada día, aprobarás el examen de conducir.
vocabulary.example_meaning: If you practise every day, you'll pass the driving test.

vocabulary.meaning: to miss (a train, a bus); to lose
vocabulary.example: Si pierdes el último metro, coge un taxi.
vocabulary.example_meaning: If you miss the last underground train, take a taxi.

vocabulary.example: Si nos damos prisa, llegamos al principio de la película.
vocabulary.example_meaning: If we hurry, we'll get there for the start of the film.

vocabulary.example: Si salimos ahora, llegamos a tiempo.
vocabulary.example_meaning: If we leave now, we'll arrive on time.

vocabulary.example: Si cambias de plan, avísame.
vocabulary.example_meaning: If you change your plans, let me know.

vocabulary.example: Si ves nubes negras, coge el paraguas.
vocabulary.example_meaning: If you see black clouds, take the umbrella.

vocabulary.meaning: to go well, to turn out well
vocabulary.example: Si todo sale bien, nos mudamos en marzo.
vocabulary.example_meaning: If all goes well, we're moving in March.

quiz.prompt: Si llueve y no llevo paraguas, siempre me ___ (mojar).
quiz.explanation: Siempre marks a general rule, so both halves are in the present: 'Si llueve…, siempre me mojo.'
hints: A habit: present + present.
Yo form of mojarse: me ___.

quiz.explanation: The si-half of a real condition takes the present indicative: 'Si estudias, aprobarás.' The future goes in the other half.
hints: Si + present, never si + future.
Tú form of estudiar.

quiz.explanation: An instruction as the result: si + present, then an imperative. With tú, the affirmative imperative of avisar is avisa, plus me attached: avísame.
hints: The second half is an order.
Pronouns attach to an affirmative imperative.

quiz.prompt: Which real condition about tomorrow is correct?
options: Si llueve mañana, nos quedamos en casa.
Si lloverá mañana, nos quedamos en casa.
Si llueva mañana, nos quedamos en casa.
quiz.correct_answer: Si llueve mañana, nos quedamos en casa.
quiz.explanation: Even when the condition is about tomorrow, si takes the present indicative. Never si + future (lloverá) or si + present subjunctive (llueva).
hints: What tense goes right after a conditional si?

quiz.prompt: Si no te das prisa, ___ el tren.
quiz.explanation: The si-half is in the present (te das), so the result can be in the future: 'perderás el tren' (you'll miss the train).
hints: The result of a real condition can be in the future.
The subjunctive and the bare infinitive don't fit here.

quiz.prompt: True or false: 'Te llamo si llego tarde' needs a comma before si.
quiz.explanation: When the si-half comes second there is no comma: 'Te llamo si llego tarde.' The comma goes after the si-half only when it comes first: 'Si llego tarde, te llamo.'
hints: Which half comes first here?

quiz.prompt: —¿Vienes a la fiesta? —___, si salgo pronto del trabajo.
quiz.explanation: The first word answers the question: yes = sí, with an accent. The si in 'si salgo pronto' means if and has no accent.
hints: Is this word 'yes' or 'if'?

quiz.prompt: Te dejo las llaves en caso de que ___ (llegar, tú) antes que yo.
quiz.explanation: En caso de que always takes the present subjunctive: llegar becomes llegues (g becomes gu before e).
hints: En caso de que is not si, and it wants the subjunctive.
Watch the spelling: -gue-.

quiz.prompt: Si todo ___ (salir) bien, vamos a llegar a tiempo.
quiz.explanation: Si + present indicative (todo sale bien), then a plan with ir a + infinitive: 'vamos a llegar a tiempo'.
hints: Todo is singular, so use the él/ella form.
Present indicative after si.

conversations.title: Plans for Saturday
conversations.scenario: Lucía and Javier plan their Saturday, but the weather forecast isn't sure yet.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: ¿Qué hacemos el sábado si hace bueno?
lines.meaning: What shall we do on Saturday if the weather's nice?

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Si hace sol, podemos subir a la sierra.
lines.meaning: If it's sunny, we can go up into the mountains.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Vale, pero el pronóstico dice que va a llover.
lines.meaning: OK, but the forecast says it's going to rain.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Pues si llueve, nos quedamos en Madrid y vamos a un museo.
lines.meaning: Well, if it rains, we'll stay in Madrid and go to a museum.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Buena idea. Si vamos al museo, invito yo a la comida.
lines.meaning: Good idea. If we go to the museum, lunch is on me.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: ¡Trato hecho! Pero si vamos a la sierra, lleva botas.
lines.meaning: Deal! But if we go to the mountains, wear boots.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Claro. Y si te levantas tarde, me voy sin ti, ¿eh?
lines.meaning: Of course. And if you get up late, I'm going without you, OK?

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Tranquila. Si pongo dos alarmas, nunca llego tarde.
lines.meaning: Don't worry. If I set two alarms, I'm never late.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Bueno, coge el paraguas en caso de que cambie el tiempo.
lines.meaning: Well, take the umbrella in case the weather changes.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Sí, y si pasa algo, te aviso por el móvil.
lines.meaning: Yes, and if anything happens, I'll let you know on my mobile.

listening.text: Si nieva, cerramos la tienda.
listening.meaning: If it snows, we close the shop.
listening.note: A general rule: present + present.

listening.text: Si tienes sueño, vete a la cama.
listening.meaning: If you're sleepy, go to bed.
listening.note: Si + present, then an imperative.

listening.text: Mañana iremos al parque si hace buen tiempo.
listening.meaning: Tomorrow we'll go to the park if the weather's good.
listening.note: No comma when the si-half comes second.

listening.text: Si Pablo no llega pronto, vamos a cenar solos.
listening.meaning: If Pablo doesn't arrive soon, we're going to have dinner on our own.
listening.note: The result can be ir a + infinitive.

listening.text: Si comes tanto chocolate, te va a doler la tripa.
listening.meaning: If you eat so much chocolate, your tummy is going to hurt.
listening.note: New word: la tripa = the tummy.

listening.text: Lleva una chaqueta en caso de que haga frío esta noche.
listening.meaning: Take a jacket in case it's cold tonight.
listening.note: En caso de que always takes the subjunctive.

listening.text: Si terminas los deberes antes de cenar, puedes jugar un rato.
listening.meaning: If you finish your homework before dinner, you can play for a while.
listening.note: New word: los deberes = the homework.

listening.text: Si pierdes las llaves otra vez, tendrás que llamar a un cerrajero.
listening.meaning: If you lose the keys again, you'll have to call a locksmith.
listening.note: New word: el cerrajero = the locksmith.

guide.tip: In English you say 'if it rains', never 'if it will rain'. Spanish si wants the plain present; put your future, order or plan in the other half.

bites.title: Si + present
bites.rule: A condition that can really happen: si + present indicative, even for tomorrow. Never si + future, never si + subjunctive.
bites.example_meaning: If it rains tomorrow, we won't go out.

bites.title: Four kinds of result
bites.rule: The other half can be a present (always true), a future, an imperative, or ir a / poder / tener que + infinitive.

bites.title: Comma or not?
bites.rule: Si-half first: a comma after it. Si-half second: no comma at all.
bites.example: Si puedo, te ayudo. Te ayudo si puedo.
bites.example_meaning: If I can, I'll help you. I'll help you if I can.

bites.title: Si or sí?
bites.rule: si without an accent = if; sí with an accent = yes. En caso de que (in case) is the one that takes the subjunctive.
bites.example_meaning: Yes, I'll go if I finish early.

sorts.title: Can it follow si?
sorts.why: After si, a real condition takes the present indicative, never the future or the subjunctive.

sorts.title: What kind of result?

items.text: Si salgo pronto, voy a ir al cine.
Si mezclas azul y amarillo, sale verde.

sorts.why: General truths use the present in both halves; plans use the future or ir a; instructions use the imperative.

spots.sentence: Si lloverá mañana, nos quedamos en casa.
spots.why: Never the future after a conditional si: si llueve.
A real condition takes the present indicative, not the subjunctive.
If = si, without an accent; sí means yes.

spots.sentence: Si estudias mucho, aprobar el examen.
spots.why: The result needs a conjugated verb: the future aprobarás.

spots.sentence: En caso de que llueve, lleva el paraguas.
spots.why: En caso de que always takes the present subjunctive.

builds.meaning: I'll call you if I'm late.

builds.text: Si hace frío, ponte el abrigo.
builds.meaning: If it's cold, put your coat on.

builds.text: Si apruebas, te invito a cenar.
builds.meaning: If you pass, I'll take you out to dinner.

realm.content:
## Si… en Eldmark

Every quest in Eldmark comes with conditions: **si entras en la mazmorra, lleva una antorcha**; **si el dragón se despierta, huimos**; **si derrotas al orco, ganarás botín**. And a wise maga always packs a potion **en caso de que haya trampas**.

vocabulary.example: Si entras en la mazmorra, lleva una antorcha.
vocabulary.example_meaning: If you go into the dungeon, take a torch.

vocabulary.example: Si pierdes la montura, tendrás que caminar hasta Highgate.
vocabulary.example_meaning: If you lose your mount, you'll have to walk to Highgate.

vocabulary.example: Si ves un orco, avisa al paladín.
vocabulary.example_meaning: If you see an orc, warn the paladin.

vocabulary.example: Llevo una poción en caso de que haya trampas.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I'm carrying a potion in case there are traps.

vocabulary.example: Si hay tormenta en Frostmarch, nos quedamos en la posada.
vocabulary.example_meaning: If there's a storm in Frostmarch, we'll stay at the inn.

vocabulary.example: La mazmorra está debajo del castillo.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The dungeon is under the castle.

vocabulary.example: Si derrotas al orco, ganarás botín.
vocabulary.example_meaning: If you defeat the orc, you'll win loot.

vocabulary.example: Si se apaga la antorcha, no vemos nada.
vocabulary.example_meaning: If the torch goes out, we can't see a thing.

vocabulary.example: Si estás herido, bebe una poción.
vocabulary.example_meaning: If you're hurt, drink a potion.

bites.title: Si en la mazmorra
bites.rule: Real dangers, real plans: si + present, then a present, a future or an order. Never si + future.
bites.example: Si abres el cofre, encontrarás botín.
bites.example_meaning: If you open the chest, you'll find loot.

listening.text: Si el orco duerme, pasamos.
listening.meaning: If the orc is asleep, we go past.
listening.note: Si + present, then present.

listening.text: Si encuentras botín, compártelo con el grupo.
listening.meaning: If you find loot, share it with the party.
listening.note: Si + present, then an imperative.

listening.text: Si la maga lanza un hechizo, todos huimos.
listening.meaning: If the mage casts a spell, we all run away.
listening.note: New word: el hechizo = the spell.

listening.text: Los enanos de Deepanvil te ayudarán si les pagas.
listening.meaning: The dwarves of Deepanvil will help you if you pay them.
listening.note: No comma when the si-half comes second.

listening.text: Si cae la noche, encendemos las antorchas.
listening.meaning: If night falls, we light the torches.

builds.meaning: If you see a dragon, run.

builds.text: Si derrotas al orco, ganarás botín.
builds.meaning: If you defeat the orc, you'll win loot.

spots.sentence: Si entrarás en la mazmorra, lleva una antorcha.
spots.why: Never the future after a conditional si.

spots.sentence: Lleva una poción en caso de que hay trampas.
spots.why: En caso de que takes the subjunctive: haya.

sorts.title: After si in Eldmark
sorts.why: After si, a real condition takes the present indicative, never the future or the subjunctive.

quiz.prompt: Si el paladín ___ a tiempo, ganaremos la batalla.
quiz.explanation: Si + present indicative, then the future: 'Si el paladín llega a tiempo, ganaremos.'
hints: What goes right after a conditional si?

quiz.explanation: Si takes the present indicative; despertar changes e to ie in se despierta.
hints: Present indicative, él form.
The stem changes e to ie.

meadowbrook.content:
## Si… en la granja

Farm life runs on real conditions: **si llueve esta semana, las fresas crecerán**; **si vas al pueblo, compra semillas en la tienda de Rosa**; **si pescas algo, Leo te lo compra**. And in autumn take a coat **en caso de que haga frío**.

vocabulary.example: Si llueve esta semana, las fresas crecerán rápido.
vocabulary.example_meaning: If it rains this week, the strawberries will grow fast.

vocabulary.example: Si la cosecha sale bien, iremos al festival con calabazas.
vocabulary.example_meaning: If the harvest goes well, we'll go to the festival with pumpkins.

vocabulary.example: Si hay tormenta, me quedo en la taberna.
vocabulary.example_meaning: If there's a storm, I'll stay at the tavern.

vocabulary.example: Si vas a la playa en otoño, lleva el paraguas.
vocabulary.example_meaning: If you go to the beach in autumn, take the umbrella.

vocabulary.example: Si pierdes la caña de pescar, Leo te presta otra.
vocabulary.example_meaning: If you lose your fishing rod, Leo will lend you another one.

vocabulary.example: La cosecha de maíz es en verano.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The maize harvest is in summer.

vocabulary.example: Si plantas estas semillas, tendrás calabazas en otoño.
vocabulary.example_meaning: If you plant these seeds, you'll have pumpkins in autumn.

vocabulary.example: Leo siempre lleva su caña de pescar al río.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Leo always takes his fishing rod to the river.

bites.title: Si en la granja
bites.rule: Plans that hang on the weather: si + present, then a present, a future, ir a or an order.
bites.example: Si hace sol, voy a plantar maíz.
bites.example_meaning: If it's sunny, I'm going to plant maize.

listening.text: Si llueve, las vacas duermen dentro.
listening.meaning: If it rains, the cows sleep inside.
listening.note: A general rule: present + present.

listening.text: Si plantas en primavera, cosecharás en verano.
listening.meaning: If you plant in spring, you'll harvest in summer.
listening.note: New word: cosechar = to harvest.

listening.text: Si ves a Nora, dale estas fresas.
listening.meaning: If you see Nora, give her these strawberries.
listening.note: Si + present, then an imperative.

listening.text: El alcalde te dará un premio si ganas.
listening.meaning: The mayor will give you a prize if you win.
listening.note: New word: el premio = the prize.

listening.text: Si la gallina pone huevos, los vendo en el mercado.
listening.meaning: If the hen lays eggs, I sell them at the market.

builds.text: Si hace sol, voy a pescar.
builds.meaning: If it's sunny, I'm going fishing.

builds.text: Si ves a Rosa, compra semillas.
builds.meaning: If you see Rosa, buy some seeds.

spots.sentence: Si hará frío, me quedo en la taberna.
spots.why: Never the future after a conditional si: si hace frío.

spots.sentence: Sí llueve, las fresas crecen rápido.

sorts.title: What comes after the comma?

items.text: Si vas al pueblo, compra pan.
Si hace frío, las gallinas no salen.
Si el río sube, la playa desaparece.
Si tienes hambre, ven a la taberna.

sorts.why: A general truth keeps the present in both halves; an instruction puts an imperative after the comma.

quiz.prompt: Si ___ mucho esta semana, las fresas crecerán.
quiz.explanation: Si + present indicative, then the future: 'Si llueve mucho, las fresas crecerán.'
hints: Never the future or the subjunctive after si.

quiz.prompt: Si la cosecha ___ (salir) bien, iremos al festival.
quiz.explanation: The si-half takes the present indicative: 'Si la cosecha sale bien, iremos al festival.'
hints: Present indicative, él/ella form.

rustwake.content:
## Si… en el páramo

Outside the Dome every plan has an if: **si hay una tormenta de ceniza, nos quedamos en el taller**; **si encuentras tuercas, cámbialas por agua filtrada**; **si suena el radiorreloj, contesta**. Leo always packs a tónico **en caso de que haya radiación**.

vocabulary.example: Si hay polvo, nos quedamos en el pueblo de chatarra.
vocabulary.example_meaning: If there's dust, we stay in the scrap town.

vocabulary.example: Si ves un escarabajo gigante, avísame por el radiorreloj.
vocabulary.example_meaning: If you see a giant beetle, let me know on the wrist radio.

vocabulary.example: Si pierdes las tuercas, no podrás comprar agua filtrada.
vocabulary.example_meaning: If you lose your nuts, you won't be able to buy filtered water.

vocabulary.example: Lleva un tónico en caso de que haya radiación.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Take a tonic in case there's radiation.

vocabulary.example: Si no nos damos prisa, la tormenta nos va a pillar.
vocabulary.example_meaning: If we don't hurry, the storm is going to catch us.

vocabulary.example: Marta cambia agua filtrada por tuercas.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Marta trades filtered water for nuts.

vocabulary.example: Si suena el radiorreloj, contesta.
vocabulary.example_meaning: If the wrist radio rings, answer.

vocabulary.example: Si llega una tormenta de ceniza, cierra la puerta.
vocabulary.example_meaning: If an ash storm comes, shut the door.

bites.title: Si en el páramo
bites.rule: Out on the plains, plan for real ifs with si + present, then a present, a future, ir a or an order. Never si + future.
bites.example: Si reparas la antena, escucharemos la radio.
bites.example_meaning: If you fix the antenna, we'll listen to the radio.

listening.text: Si hay polvo, cierro la puerta.
listening.meaning: If there's dust, I shut the door.
listening.note: A general rule: present + present.

listening.text: Si Marta tiene agua filtrada, le compramos dos botellas.
listening.meaning: If Marta has filtered water, we'll buy two bottles from her.

listening.text: Si el robot jardinero falla, repáralo.
listening.meaning: If the robot gardener breaks down, fix it.
listening.note: New word: fallar = to break down.

listening.text: Leo vendrá al mercado si no hay tormenta.
listening.meaning: Leo will come to the market if there's no storm.
listening.note: No comma when the si-half comes second.

listening.text: Si encuentras chatarra útil, llévala al taller.
listening.meaning: If you find useful scrap, take it to the workshop.
listening.note: New word: útil = useful.

builds.text: Si hay radiación, bebe un tónico.
builds.meaning: If there's radiation, drink a tonic.

builds.text: Te aviso si veo una cabra.
builds.meaning: I'll let you know if I see a goat.

spots.sentence: Si encontrarás tuercas, cámbialas por agua.
spots.why: Never the future after a conditional si: si encuentras.

spots.sentence: En caso de que llega la tormenta, quédate en el taller.
spots.why: En caso de que takes the present subjunctive: llegue.

sorts.title: What does the other half do?

items.text: Si hay tormenta, vamos a esperar.
Si tienes sed, bebe agua filtrada.
Si reparo la antena, escucharemos música.
Si Marta abre el mercado, compraré gaseosa Zafiro.

sorts.why: After the si-half, an imperative gives an order; the future or ir a + infinitive gives a plan.

quiz.prompt: Si ___ una tormenta de ceniza, nos quedamos en el taller.
quiz.explanation: Si + present indicative: hay. Not habrá (future) or haya (subjunctive).
hints: What tense goes right after a conditional si?

quiz.prompt: Si ___ (encontrar, tú) tuercas, cámbialas por agua filtrada.
quiz.explanation: Si + present indicative, then an imperative. Encontrar changes o to ue in encuentras.
hints: Present indicative, tú form.
The stem changes o to ue.

conversations.title: The antenna job
conversations.scenario: Foreman Ruiz offers Leo the scavenger a job to fix the old antenna before the ash storm arrives.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Leo, si reparas la antena hoy, te pago veinte tuercas.
lines.meaning: Leo, if you fix the antenna today, I'll pay you twenty nuts.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: ¿Y si llega una tormenta de ceniza?
lines.meaning: And what if an ash storm comes?

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Si hay tormenta, te quedas en el taller y esperas.
lines.meaning: If there's a storm, you stay in the workshop and wait.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Vale. Y si veo escarabajos gigantes, ¿qué hago?
lines.meaning: OK. And if I see giant beetles, what do I do?

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Si ves alguno, avísame por el radiorreloj.
lines.meaning: If you see one, let me know on the wrist radio.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: De acuerdo. Llevo un tónico en caso de que haya radiación.
lines.meaning: All right. I'll take a tonic in case there's radiation.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Bien pensado. Y si todo sale bien, te invito a una gaseosa Zafiro.
lines.meaning: Good thinking. And if all goes well, the Zafiro soda is on me.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: ¡Trato hecho! Si me doy prisa, vuelvo antes de la cena.
lines.meaning: Deal! If I hurry, I'll be back before dinner.
